claims.statement: Box documents a client secret as a value held by the application that requests, refreshes or revokes an OAuth 2.0 access token, sent together with the client ID. Existence only: no prefix, alphabet, length or checksum is established.

sources.supports: The client secret of the application requesting an access token. (token request); The client secret of the application requesting to refresh the token. (refresh request)

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Is the one client secret that the specification names for the authorization-code, client-credentials and JWT-bearer grants a single credential across Box application types, or do application types (OAuth 2.0, server authentication with client credentials or JWT, platform apps) issue differently shaped or differently scoped secrets? Needs the developer documentation, which was not readable.
Which prefix, alphabet and length, if any, does the provider state? The specification's example value is an example, not a format statement, and no format claim is recorded.
